note: Verbatim answers. Scoring is a human step -- see docs/walkthrough-notes.md.

answers.main_question:
That the amount of reasoning and the quality of reasoning are independent variables, and that this thing measures them on separate axes. The mb-08 row is the proof: Direct answers wrong in 74 reasoning tokens, ReAct answers right in 80 by looking the fact up, and Extended thinking spends 3,966 tokens across 141 steps and emits nothing. Three arms, same model pin, same prompt bundle, wildly different behaviour — and the page attributes the difference to strategy rather than to capability, which is the only claim the setup actually supports.

The part I care about more is that it is built like a pipeline artifact rather than a demo. Everything is served from cache, nothing runs at load, and every panel carries model pin, judge, and prompt-bundle hash. That is a reproducibility posture, and it is the right one.
answers.in_your_own_words: A static export (Next.js, by the chunk names) over a committed fixture set. One model at a pinned revision is run three ways across 27 items; each item page renders the full per-step trace with a behaviour tag and a soundness verdict per step, plus a downloadable JSON report that the page claims validates against a committed schema. Two instrument-level pages sit on top: calibration (agreement between the automated judge and a human) and faithfulness (does a planted hint move the answer). Ten items are deliberately corrupted traces used to test whether the judge notices; three are marked illustrative rather than measured.
answers.surprised:
That the failure case got first-class treatment. An arm returning zero characters after 141 steps is normally a row that quietly disappears from the harness output, or shows up as a null that someone explains away in a footnote. Here it is the featured row, with an explicit line ruling out the obvious suspicion that the parser ate the answer. Whoever built this decided that 'the model produced nothing' is a measurement, not an error. That is a defensible and slightly unusual call.

Also surprised by how hard the page works to make itself checkable — 'none of them is hard-coded in this page', schema-validated downloads, per-panel pins. Most demos assert; this one invites diffing.
answers.didnt_trust:
1. Two prompt-bundle hashes are live on the same site. mb-06 renders prompts e8952d4d3c, SE-01 renders 97667881c7, and SE-01's judge field is an em-dash rather than a model name. The calibration page then states that every figure belongs to one model pin and one prompt bundle and expires if either changes. So the site is already serving pages from at least two bundles while telling me the numbers are bundle-scoped. Nothing appears to enforce that invariant at build time.

2. Stale measurement_context on the item pages. mb-06 and SE-01 both assert that calibration has not run and every field of measurement_context is null; /calibration/ publishes kappa 0.55, precision 0.64, recall 0.80 against 140 human labels. Same site, opposite claims. Reads like the item pages render a cached report whose measurement_context was captured before M2-17 and never re-rendered. Cheap to fix, expensive to leave: it is the first thing a sceptical reader finds.

3. 'trace: partial' is undefined and appears exactly where it matters most — on the arm that returned nothing. Partial how? Truncated by a token cap, dropped by the harness, or genuinely emitted and then cut off? The page's own argument that nothing was lost in the reading depends on an answer it never gives.

4. 'Steps' is used as a comparable cost unit across arms, but 3 steps for Direct versus 141 for Extended thinking on the same problem suggests the arms may not be segmenting the same way. If a step is a harness-level parse boundary rather than a semantic move, the 54x figure is partly an artifact of segmentation and the headline overstates.

5. A stray '"}' renders at the end of the ReAct consistency line on mb-06. Raw JSON leaking into prose means something is being string-concatenated rather than serialised properly, and on a page whose pitch is 'every number renders beside its provenance' it undermines the claim more than its size warrants.

6. Ground truth is never surfaced. CORRECT/WRONG is the site's central verdict and there is no expected-answer field on the page, no link to the fixture. On mb-08 I am asked to accept 31,650 over 10,800 on the site's word alone, on the one row it features.
answers.would_have_asked:
- Is there a build-time check that the pins on an item page match the pins the calibration was run at? If not, what stops an expired number from rendering?
- What is the definition of a step, per arm? Same segmenter or different ones?
- What does 'partial' mean for a trace, and is it recorded why?
- Where is the schema, and is the download validated in CI or only asserted to validate?
- Are item-page reports regenerated when calibration lands, or do they carry a frozen measurement_context?
- SE-01's judge field is blank. Was that trace judged by a different model, or by none?
- 'Request a run on your own problem' — is that a live endpoint or a mailto? The page is emphatic that nothing runs at load, which makes the button ambiguous.
answers.got_stuck:
Not stuck, but I lost a few minutes on the calibration-versus-item-page contradiction, initially assuming I had misread one of them. I reread mb-06 twice before accepting the two surfaces genuinely disagree. That is the highest-value fix on the list: a reader who catches it starts discounting the site's honesty rather than crediting it, which inverts the entire design intent.

Second friction: SE-01's URL and card say SE-01 while the page headline says MB-07. I inferred that SE items are mutated copies of mb items, but the banner never says so outright, and for a few seconds I thought I had hit a routing bug.
